{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Confirm no QA orders (despite documentation)
qa_orders = data[data['revenue'] == '999999.99']
assert len(qa_orders) == 0, "QA orders found, contradicting data"

# Filter out refunded orders — they should not be counted in conversion rate
# Conversion rate is defined as: number of converted orders / total orders (only completed)
# But note: 'converted' is 1 only if order completed checkout
# So we keep only 'completed' orders for conversion rate calculation
completed_orders = data[data['status'] == 'completed']

# Check revenue format — it's string with commas
print("Sample revenue values after parsing:")
# Strip commas and convert to float
completed_orders['revenue_float'] = completed_orders['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
print(completed_orders['revenue_float'].head())

# Check distribution of channels and segments
print("\nChannel distribution:")
print(completed_orders['channel'].value_counts())

print("\nCustomer segment distribution:")
print(completed_orders['customer_segment'].value_counts())

# Check cross-tab of channel vs segment — this is critical
print("\nCross-tabulation of channel vs customer_segment:")
print(pd.crosstab(completed_orders['channel'], completed_orders['customer_segment']))"}
